newsitem.title: UK: HSBC Gibbs moves into marine reinsurance.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Gibbs moves into marine reinsurance.

text.p: International insurance broker HSBC Gibbs, a part of HSBC Holdings plc, said on Monday it has expanded into the marine reinsurance broking market.

Two marine reinsurers, Michael Vandervord and Andrew Hinds, have been recruited by HSBC Gibbs, the company said in a statement, adding that the move completes the package of services offered by its marine division.

Peter Ahlas, chief executive of HSBC Gibb's marine, cargo and aviation division, declined to say how much business the expansion would generate, but told Reuters, "I hope the impact will be significant."
Ahlas said the company had moved into marine reinsurance because it saw opportunities to build on its marine insurance operations.
HSBC Gibbs also expects to benefit from any recovery in marine reinsurance, which traditionally experiences an upturn in rates before marine insurance.
Marine rates have been falling sharply and remain soft.
In 1995, HSBC Gibb generated profits of 15 million stg on revenue of 83 million stg. It is among the top 25 insurance brokers in the world.
The company provides a wide range of broking services including personal lines, treaty reinsurance, political risk, directors and officers, school fees insurance and a benefits consultancy.
